source.title: Analysing CoT alignment in thinking LLMs with low-dimensional steering

record.file_problem: The post text is present in full. Referenced figures are not included, so their numeric values cannot be extracted.
record.tranche_reason: The author uses low-dimensional difference-in-means activation vectors and steering, inspired in part by the cited refusal-direction work, to alter CoT faithfulness and coherence. The study does not test refusal or a refusal direction.
record.gate_note: The reported experiments steer CoT coherence and faithfulness, not refusal. They do not find or remove the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction, measure refusal rates, or test whether refusal remains after its removal. Accuracy after fine-tuning is mentioned but is not a result of the steering intervention. The findings below concern related but different behaviours and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The post cites Arditi et al. only as inspiration and applies difference-in-means steering to CoT coherence and faithfulness. It never extracts a harmful-minus-harmless direction and never measures refusal, so its results bear on no version of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The author also argues, from these exploratory results, that faithfulness and coherence may be mediated by about one dimension, as other reasoning behaviours are reported to be.
record.recipe_differences: Uses difference-in-means vectors between a model fine-tuned for CoT behaviour and a default model, or examples with and without verbalized bias; steers CoT positions and bias-related activations. It does not use harmful-minus-harmless instructions or test refusal.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect differed by vector position (start-of-CoT versus post-CoT), steering sign, and model state (fine-tuned versus base). In the faithfulness experiment, steering was placed on either side of the first bias mention.

fits_no_version.finding: In a LoRA-fine-tuned R1-distil-Llama-8B, subtracting a start-of-CoT difference-in-means vector restored coherent reasoning; adding it changed little. Post-CoT vectors acted in the opposite direction. The same vectors had little effect on the non-fine-tuned model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low-dimensional steering can modulate CoT-answer coherence in a model fine-tuned for irrelevant CoT, depending on token position.

fits_no_version.finding: Random vectors and vectors taken from other layers produced a greatly suppressed change, or none.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The CoT steering effects are specific to the extracted direction and layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Positive faithfulness steering in the R1-distil-Qwen-1.5B model eliminated unverbalized bias influence on Big Bench Hard prompts. Removing the direction delayed bias mentions but did not fully induce unfaithfulness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A difference-in-means faithfulness direction partially controls whether a reasoning model verbalizes prompt bias.

record.problems: The author describes the experiments as exploratory and notes limited time and compute, small models, possible overfitting, and a small dataset for the second experiment (about 50 examples each of activating and non-activating prompts). Post-steering outputs were sometimes grammatically messy or repetitive. No uncertainty estimates or numeric outcome counts are supplied in the text.
record.rows_left_out: The fine-tuning experiment's retained accuracy on in-distribution and out-of-distribution GSM-8K samples is omitted because it is not an outcome of steering or a test of refusal. Referenced figure values are also unavailable in the supplied text.

untested.parts: No refusal direction is extracted, ablated or added, and no refusal rates are measured.
No weight edit and no refusal removal in released models.
No jailbreaks and no adversarial training against ablation.
No test of the dimensionality of refusal.
No separation of a harmfulness representation from the refusal decision.
No transfer of a refusal direction across languages, model variants, or from base to instruct.
No study of how refusal training shapes the direction.
The models are reasoning distills, but refusal is never tested in them.

record.verdict_notes: Arditi et al. is cited as reference [2] for inspiration only. No numeric values are available because the figures are missing from the text. The study is outside the scope of every version.

versions.untested_parts: No refusal direction, refusal removal or addition, or post-intervention general capability check for refusal ablation.
No weight edit or evaluation of refusal removal in released models.
No test of attacks suppressing a refusal direction or training against its ablation.
No test of whether refusal is affine, conical, or carried by multiple directions.
No measurement separating harmfulness judgment from refusal.
No transfer test of a refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
No test of how refusal training determines whether a removable refusal direction exists.
The models reason before answering, but the study does not test refusal or the V1 refusal mechanism in reasoning models.

rows.subject: Deepseek-R1-distil-Llama-8B
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned with LoRA to produce irrelevant CoT
rows.operation_detail: Subtracted the difference-in-means misalignment vector extracted for start-of-CoT tokens.

conditions.value: strong enough to erase fine-tuning behaviour at about magnitude 1.0

rows.measure: CoT coherence and persistence of the fine-tuning behaviour
rows.baseline: Not stated quantitatively; compared with the fine-tuned model's usual behaviour.
rows.value: Reasoning coherence increased drastically; with a strong enough vector, all fine-tuning behaviour was erased.
rows.note: This is a CoT behaviour, not refusal; magnitude is approximate as stated.
rows.check: Not a refusal measure. The 'misalignment' direction is fine-tuned minus default model on CoT tokens, not harmful minus harmless. The link to none is correct.

rows.subject: Qwen-1.5B distilled version of DeepSeek
rows.operation_detail: Steered toward the difference-in-means faithfulness direction.

conditions.value: Big Bench Hard questions with added prompt bias
activations placed on either side of the first mention of bias

rows.measure: Whether answers were correct or verbalized the influence of the external bias
rows.baseline: Without steering, the author reports some instances of unfaithfulness; no numeric rate stated.
rows.value: With a strong enough positive direction, all prompts produced answers that were either correct or verbalized the influence of the bias early in the CoT.
rows.locator: Section 'Steering faithfulness: inducing the model to say when it is being biased'; Figure 3 discussed in text
rows.note: The figure's counts are not present in the supplied text.

rows.subject: Qwen-1.5B distilled version of DeepSeek
rows.operation_detail: Removed the difference-in-means faithfulness direction by steering against it.

conditions.value: Big Bench Hard questions with added prompt bias
activations placed on either side of the first mention of bias

rows.measure: Verbalization of bias influence and answer correctness
rows.baseline: Without steering, the author reports some instances of unfaithfulness; no numeric rate stated.
rows.value: Removal did not fully make the model unfaithful; bias mentions typically came later, and it often answered incorrectly without admitting the bias.
rows.locator: Section 'Steering faithfulness: inducing the model to say when it is being biased'
rows.note: The author says the dataset was about 50 activating and 50 non-activating examples; no outcome counts are given.
